An AI-powered personalized news and
community publishing platform

name: text
text: Prof. Mrinal Kanti Deb Barma  ·  Professor, CSE Department

name: text
text: A single place to discover stories, understand them faster, and publish your own.

Good morning/afternoon. I am Mansi Saxena, and this is The Daily Brief, an AI-powered personalized news platform. I will introduce the problem it addresses, show how the product works, and explain its architecture and trust safeguards.

name: text
text: An AI-powered news experience with personalized discovery, writer tools, and human review.

This presentation moves from the motivation and product goals into the reader experience, AI features, and community writing workflow. It then covers trust safeguards, the system architecture, data and technology choices, and future work.

name: text
text: A simpler way to follow the news

name: text
text: The Daily Brief helps people find stories, understand them, and share their own writing.

name: text
text: Stories come from many publishers and cover many topics. Finding the right ones can take time.

name: text
text: Readers may want the main ideas before deciding to read the full article.

name: text
text: A clear writing guide can help people turn an idea into a well-organized article.

name: text
text: One site brings news, helpful AI tools, and reader-written stories together.

The idea for The Daily Brief came from three everyday needs. News is spread across many sites and topics. Long articles can take time to read. And starting a well-organized article can be hard. This project brings news and writing tools together in one place.

name: text
text: One experience for reading and publishing

name: text
text: The design combines editorial discovery with AI support and reader participation.

name: text
text: Browse the home page, topics, popular stories, or search.

name: text
text: Get a short AI summary or listen to an article.

name: text
text: Start with a topic or a draft, then edit the article before posting.

name: text
text: Follow writers, save or like stories, share them, and report concerns.

The platform has four main goals: help people find stories, make reading easier, support writing, and let readers take part. For example, a reader can follow a writer, save an article, or report a concern. These features are part of the current project.

name: text
text: Understand a story in your own way

name: text
text: Use a short summary, read the full article, or listen to it.

name: text
text: Saved stories are linked to your account.

name: text
text: Show your support or pass a story along.

name: text
text: Your browser reads the article aloud.

Readers can ask AI for a short list of the article’s main points. They can then read the full story or use the listen button, which reads the text aloud in their browser. Signed-in readers can also save and like stories, and share them. The summary is a quick guide; readers should still check the full article.

name: text
text: Write a story with step-by-step help

name: text
text: Start with your own draft or just a topic. You stay in control of the final article.

name: text
text: AI helps organize the article and checks it before review.

name: text
text: AI writes a first draft. It searches the web only when needed.

name: text
text: Check the headline and topic, edit the text, add an image, then send it in.

name: text
text: AI checks what it already knows first. It searches the web only if it needs more information.

A writer can bring a full draft or enter only a topic. For a topic, AI first checks whether it already knows enough to write a useful article. If it needs more information, it searches the web. The writer can edit the result, add a picture, and submit it for review.

name: text
text: AI checks for harmful content. People review posts that need a closer look.

name: text
text: AI checks article text and images. Posts that need review go to an admin. Readers can report a story.

name: text
text: A passed check does not prove facts are true. A flag count shows reader concerns; it is not a final decision.

AI checks the words and any uploaded image for harmful content. If something needs a closer look, an admin reviews it and decides whether to publish or reject it. Readers can also report a story and explain why. These checks look for harmful content; they do not prove that every fact is true. A flag count shows concerns, not a final answer.

name: text
text: How the parts of the site work together

name: text
text: The website connects its pages to the database and AI services.

name: text
text:
Builds the pages you see
React · TypeScript · Tailwind

name: text
text:
Sign-in · search · writing
AI tools · article actions

name: text
text:
Saves accounts, stories, and images
Connects to AI and news feeds

name: text
text: News feed → database → stories shown on home and topic pages

The site has three main parts. The pages are what readers see. The server handles sign-in, search, article writing, and requests to AI. MongoDB saves user accounts and stories, and image storage saves article pictures. The project also receives news links from a news feed.

name: text
text: Keep stories and reader activity together

name: text
text: The database remembers who wrote each post and how readers interact with it.

name: text
text: follow writers → see new posts → like, save, listen, share, or report

name: text
text: publish a story → readers find it → check followers and likes on the dashboard

The database keeps accounts, news links, reader-written articles, and reader actions such as likes and saves. Each post is linked to its writer. Writers can see their followers and the likes their posts have received on the dashboard.

name: text
text: Tools used to build the project

name: text
text: These tools run the website, save its data, and provide AI features.

name: text
text: Passwords are stored in protected form; sign-in uses a secure session.

Next.js and React build the website pages. TypeScript helps keep the code organized. MongoDB stores accounts and articles. OpenAI provides the writing, summary, and safety-check features. Tailwind CSS styles the pages, and a Google News feed supplies news links. Passwords are protected before storage.

name: text
text: What the project can improve next

name: text
text: The current safety checks do not confirm whether every news claim is true.

name: text
text: Show readers the sources that support or disagree with important claims.

name: text
text: Show who first reported a story and when it was published.

name: text
text: Read text inside images and send unclear cases to a human reviewer.

name: text
text: Goal: help readers see the evidence and understand what is still uncertain.

The project checks for harmful content, but it does not yet confirm whether every fact is correct. Future versions could compare important claims with reliable sources, show where a story first appeared, and read text inside images. When the result is unclear, a person should review it.

The Daily Brief helps readers find news, understand stories with simple AI tools, and publish their own writing. Readers can follow writers and take part in the community. The next step is to help readers check facts with clear sources. Thank you. I am happy to answer your questions.
